output.brief: The remote promotion gap is mostly a difference in time in level, not where people work. Remote hiring only opened widely in July 2024. About 215 of the 340 remote staff started in March 2025 or later, so only 32% of remote staff were eligible (18+ months in level), against 74% of office staff. Among eligible people, nomination rates (28% vs 29%), approval rates (71% vs 74%) and promotion rates (20% vs 21%) are almost the same. Applying office rates to the remote eligibility mix predicts 8.2%, against the 7.6% observed. That is a small gap, but only 110 remote staff are eligible, so a real difference of a few points can't be ruled out. Attrition isn't higher for remote staff. Job-family mix doesn't explain the gap. Stretch-work access is unmeasured; manager comments hint at a proximity effect, so it's still worth checking. Don't confirm proximity bias or announce the three-day rule. It would target people hired on home-based contracts, about 180 of whom live over 150 km from an office, and it rests on a misread comparison. Put it on hold. Report promotion rates for eligible staff only. Collect staffing and nomination data, then re-check at FY2027.
output.methodChoice: Collected X10 (eligibility-adjusted outcomes) and X15 (hiring dates and attrition) to test the tenure confounder and the attrition rival.
